answer: Divergent history challenge.** Each identity must publish a signed, ever-growing local log of random challenges it solved. Verification asks an identity to answer a fresh challenge derived from its own log; a clone sharing the log cannot answer challenges seeded by the original's private divergences, so copies collapse to one voice. To field N identities, an attacker must run N truly separate histories, paying N times the ongoing compute and storage — an island of effort per identity, not one voyage duplicated. This fable costs clones their cheapness.
